primary_citation: 18 U.S.C. §2511 (Title III of the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968, Pub. L. 90-351; amended by ECPA, Pub. L. 99-508 (1986))
short_title: Wiretap Act / ECPA Title I — Prohibition on Interception of Wire and Electronic Communications; Civil Remedy
one_line_rule: Intentional interception of wire, oral, or electronic communications in transit is prohibited; any person whose communications are intercepted may sue for the greater of actual damages or $10,000 per violation, plus punitive damages and attorneys' fees.

case_law.court: Supreme Court of the United States
case_law.key_rule: §2511(1)(c) covers disclosure of intercepted communications (not just interception); narrow First Amendment public concern exception; private communications (financial, medical, personal) fully protected; each disclosure = separate violation.

case_law.cite: Jewel v. National Security Agency, 673 F.3d 902 (9th Cir. 2011)
case_law.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
case_law.key_rule: Carrier maintenance exception (§2511(2)(a)(i)) is narrow — normal course of business + necessary to service; fraudulent SIM port outside maintenance exception; standing for each individual whose communications were intercepted.

sim_swap_application.theory: SIM swap routes incoming calls and SMS to attacker's device in real-time = interception during transmission = §2511(1)(a)
sim_swap_application.disclosure_chain: Each conspiracy member who received and acted on intercepted communications = §2511(1)(c) disclosure liability; $10,000 per disclosure
sim_swap_application.cipa_stack: California CIPA §632/§637.2 runs simultaneously: $5,000/violation or 3× actual; all-party consent not met
sim_swap_application.damages_per_interception: Federal: $10,000 minimum; California: $5,000 minimum; stacked per communication event
sim_swap_application.defendants: Ryan McClaran (interceptor); Christina Cerretani and others who received/used intercepted content (§2511(1)(c) disclosure)
sim_swap_application.sol: 2 years from discovery; each interception event = fresh violation
